newsitem.title: SPAIN: Argentaria sinks after 5 pct margin fall.
newsitem.headline: Argentaria sinks after 5 pct margin fall.

text.p: Shares in Spain's Argentaria were down sharply on Thursday after the bank posted a 13.1 percent fall in net profit and a 5.4 percent drop in net interest income during the nine months to September, dealers said.
At 1040 GMT Argentaria was down 100 pesetas, 1.98 percent, to 4,950. The Ibex-35 index was off 0.04 percent to 4,306.90

"The results were surprisingly bad and people don't see any way out of it. In the loan market they're not looking good and there's talk that they might buy back capital," said a trader at a Spanish brokerage who requested anonymity.
Argentaria was not immediately available for comment.

On Wednesday the bank said net attibutable profit fell 13.1 percent to 48.55 billion pesetas. Customer loans fell 1.8 percent, in line with a new strategy which aimed to "prioritise profitability over size," the bank said.
The trader commented: "Their return on capital (0.54 percent) has deteriorated, they're overly staffed. They're going to have to restructure. It's just a dead weight."
He set a target range of 4,600-4,800 pesetas for the stock.

A second trader at a major Spanish bank said "The results were much worse than expected. There's a change of strategy with the new management and it looks like they're cleaning up the balance sheet ahead of the privatisation."
The government is due to sell its remaining 25 percent stake in the bank in principle by summer 1997.
In a Reuter survey last week, analysts forecast on average a 0.03 percent fall in Argentaria's attributable profit for the first nine months of the year.
